title: Choose the visual direction
question: I’ve kept your dark, institutional finance-dashboard brief as the lead. Choose it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Institutional Research Sheet
options.thesis: Put each screening result beside its unit, status, and data provenance.
options.viewport: A persistent horizontal navigation, compact ticker search, screening evidence, and a Historical Comparison chart with a metric selector and LIVE or SYNTHETIC DEMO state.
options.risk: Dense data can blur the difference between synthetic history and verified live evidence.

raised.raise: Every plotted series keeps its units and LIVE or SYNTHETIC DEMO provenance in view.

options.label: Market Close Dispatch
options.thesis: Lead with the selected company’s current screen and the evidence behind it.
options.viewport: A slim header and top navigation lead into a compact evidence table; a chart rail below compares one selected metric by year.
options.risk: A bulletin rhythm can make monitoring history feel secondary to the latest snapshot.

options.label: Data Lattice
options.thesis: Make annual metric movement the most legible visual in the workspace.
options.viewport: The familiar finance workspace remains intact; fine annual markers and a restrained line grid focus attention on the selected metric.
options.case: Strong investor identification through data density; less direct on the meaning and provenance of the screening evidence.
options.risk: A decorative lattice can compete with the actual values.

options.label: Evidence Pairs
options.thesis: Pair every conclusion with the evidence and source that support it.
options.viewport: Each criterion sits beside its observation and source; the history chart follows as a separate, explicitly labeled comparison.
options.case: Keeps evidence close to every conclusion; its marketing-oriented pairing is less native to a dense research workflow.
options.risk: Repeating labels beside every value may add unnecessary density.

options.label: Character Roster
options.thesis: Use a memorable roster to make demo companies easy to recognize.
options.viewport: The required finance workspace stays standard; demo fixtures appear as a scanable company list.
options.case: Weak investor identification and a roster does not clarify historical financial evidence.
options.kept: A short, scannable list of named demo fixtures.
options.risk: Character styling would undermine the institutional research tone.

options.label: Guide-Map Legend
options.thesis: Make each metric’s status easy to locate in a clear legend.
options.viewport: Standard top navigation and research panels remain in place, with a persistent legend clarifying units and data state.
options.case: Its map metaphor is unfamiliar for equity screening and does not improve the required chart.
options.kept: Keep a compact legend for units and LIVE, unavailable, or synthetic data.
options.risk: A spatial-map metaphor could make ordinary metrics feel like locations.

canonCard.label: Institutional Dashboard
canonCard.thesis: Deliver the familiar dark research workspace directly, without a borrowed metaphor.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional top navigation, ticker field, criteria table, and interactive historical comparison.
canonCard.risk: The familiar category pattern needs meticulous hierarchy to avoid looking generic.
